NKJV.1: The word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
NKJV.2: Now it shall come to pass in the latter days That the mountain of the LORD’s house Shall be established on the top of the mountains, And shall be exalted above the hills; And all nations shall flow to it.
NKJV.3: Many people shall come and say,  “Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, To the house of the God of Jacob; He will teach us His ways, And we shall walk in His paths.”  For out of Zion shall go forth the law, And the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
NKJV.4: He shall judge between the nations, And rebuke many people; They shall beat their swords into plowshares, And their spears into pruning hooks; Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, Neither shall they learn war anymore.
NKJV.5: O house of Jacob, come and let us walk In the light of the LORD.
NKJV.6: For You have forsaken Your people, the house of Jacob, Because they are filled with eastern ways; They are soothsayers like the Philistines, And they are pleased with the children of foreigners.
NKJV.7: Their land is also full of silver and gold, And there is no end to their treasures; Their land is also full of horses, And there is no end to their chariots.
NKJV.8: Their land is also full of idols; They worship the work of their own hands, That which their own fingers have made.
NKJV.9: People bow down, And each man humbles himself; Therefore do not forgive them.
NKJV.10: Enter into the rock, and hide in the dust, From the terror of the LORD And the glory of His majesty.
NKJV.11: The lofty looks of man shall be humbled, The haughtiness of men shall be bowed down, And the LORD alone shall be exalted in that day.
NKJV.12: For the day of the LORD of hosts Shall come upon everything proud and lofty, Upon everything lifted up— And it shall be brought low—
NKJV.13: Upon all the cedars of Lebanon that are high and lifted up, And upon all the oaks of Bashan;
NKJV.14: Upon all the high mountains, And upon all the hills that are lifted up;
NKJV.15: Upon every high tower, And upon every fortified wall;
NKJV.16: Upon all the ships of Tarshish, And upon all the beautiful sloops.
NKJV.17: The loftiness of man shall be bowed down, And the haughtiness of men shall be brought low; The LORD alone will be exalted in that day,
NKJV.18: But the idols He shall utterly abolish.
NKJV.19: They shall go into the holes of the rocks, And into the caves of the earth,  From the terror of the LORD And the glory of His majesty, When He arises to shake the earth mightily.
NKJV.20: In that day a man will cast away his idols of silver And his idols of gold, Which they made, each for himself to worship, To the moles and bats,
NKJV.21: To go into the clefts of the rocks, And into the crags of the rugged rocks, From the terror of the LORD And the glory of His majesty, When He arises to shake the earth mightily.
NKJV.22: Sever yourselves from such a man, Whose breath is in his nostrils; For of what account is he?

ESV.1: The word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
ESV.2: It shall come to pass in the latter days that the mountain of the house of the LORD shall be established as the highest of the mountains, and shall be lifted up above the hills; and all the nations shall flow to it,
ESV.3: and many peoples shall come, and say: “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob, that he may teach us his ways and that we may walk in his paths.” For out of Zion shall go forth the law,  and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
ESV.4: He shall judge between the nations, and shall decide disputes for many peoples; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks; nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war anymore.
ESV.5: O house of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the LORD.
ESV.6: For you have rejected your people, the house of Jacob, because they are full of things from the east and of fortune-tellers like the Philistines, and they strike hands with the children of foreigners.
ESV.7: Their land is filled with silver and gold, and there is no end to their treasures; their land is filled with horses, and there is no end to their chariots.
ESV.8: Their land is filled with idols; they bow down to the work of their hands, to what their own fingers have made.
ESV.9: So man is humbled, and each one is brought low — do not forgive them!
ESV.10: Enter into the rock and hide in the dust from before the terror of the LORD, and from the splendor of his majesty.
ESV.11: The haughty looks of man shall be brought low, and the lofty pride of men shall be humbled, and the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.
ESV.12: For the LORD of hosts has a day against all that is proud and lofty, against all that is lifted up — and it shall be brought low;
ESV.13: against all the cedars of Lebanon, lofty and lifted up; and against all the oaks of Bashan;
ESV.14: against all the lofty mountains, and against all the uplifted hills;
ESV.15: against every high tower, and against every fortified wall;
ESV.16: against all the ships of Tarshish, and against all the beautiful craft.
ESV.17: And the haughtiness of man shall be humbled, and the lofty pride of men shall be brought low, and the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.
ESV.18: And the idols shall utterly pass away.
ESV.19: And people shall enter the caves of the rocks and the holes of the ground,  from before the terror of the LORD, and from the splendor of his majesty, when he rises to terrify the earth.
ESV.20: In that day mankind will cast away their idols of silver and their idols of gold, which they made for themselves to worship, to the moles and to the bats,
ESV.21: to enter the caverns of the rocks and the clefts of the cliffs, from before the terror of the LORD, and from the splendor of his majesty, when he rises to terrify the earth.
ESV.22: Stop regarding man in whose nostrils is breath, for of what account is he?

NASB.1: The word which Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
NASB.2: Now it will come about that In the last days The mountain of the house of the LORD Will be established as the chief of the mountains, And will be raised above the hills; And all the nations will stream to it.
NASB.3: And many peoples will come and say, 'Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, To the house of the God of Jacob; That He may teach us concerning His ways And that we may walk in His paths.' For the law will go forth from Zion And the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
NASB.4: And He will judge between the nations, And will render decisions for many peoples; And they will hammer their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not lift up sword against nation, And never again will they learn war.
NASB.5: Come, house of Jacob, and let us walk in the light of the LORD.
NASB.6: For You have abandoned Your people, the house of Jacob, Because they are filled [with influences] from the east, And [they are] soothsayers like the Philistines, And they strike [bargains] with the children of foreigners.
NASB.7: Their land has also been filled with silver and gold And there is no end to their treasures; Their land has also been filled with horses And there is no end to their chariots.
NASB.8: Their land has also been filled with idols; They worship the work of their hands, That which their fingers have made.
NASB.9: So the [common] man has been humbled And the man [of importance] has been abased, But do not forgive them.
NASB.10: Enter the rock and hide in the dust From the terror of the LORD and from the splendor of His majesty.
NASB.11: The proud look of man will be abased And the loftiness of man will be humbled, And the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.
NASB.12: For the LORD of hosts will have a day [of reckoning] Against everyone who is proud and lofty And against everyone who is lifted up, That he may be abased.
NASB.13: And [it will be] against all the cedars of Lebanon that are lofty and lifted up, Against all the oaks of Bashan,
NASB.14: Against all the lofty mountains, Against all the hills that are lifted up,
NASB.15: Against every high tower, Against every fortified wall,
NASB.16: Against all the ships of Tarshish And against all the beautiful craft.
NASB.17: The pride of man will be humbled And the loftiness of men will be abased; And the LORD alone will be exalted in that day,
NASB.18: But the idols will completely vanish.
NASB.19: [Men] will go into caves of the rocks And into holes of the ground Before the terror of the LORD And the splendor of His majesty, When He arises to make the earth tremble.
NASB.20: In that day men will cast away to the moles and the bats Their idols of silver and their idols of gold, Which they made for themselves to worship,
NASB.21: In order to go into the caverns of the rocks and the clefts of the cliffs Before the terror of the LORD and the splendor of His majesty, When He arises to make the earth tremble.
NASB.22: Stop regarding man, whose breath [of life] is in his nostrils; For why should he be esteemed?

NLT.1: This is a vision that Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem:
NLT.2:
In the last days, the mountain of the LORD’s house
will be the highest of all —
the most important place on earth.
It will be raised above the other hills,
and people from all over the world will stream there to worship.
NLT.3:
People from many nations will come and say,
“Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD,
to the house of Jacob’s God.
There he will teach us his ways,
and we will walk in his paths.”
For the LORD’s teaching will go out from Zion;
his word will go out from Jerusalem.
NLT.4:
The LORD will mediate between nations
and will settle international disputes.
They will hammer their swords into plowshares
and their spears into pruning hooks.
Nation will no longer fight against nation,
nor train for war anymore.
NLT.5:
Come, descendants of Jacob,
let us walk in the light of the LORD!
NLT.6:
For the LORD has rejected his people,
the descendants of Jacob,
because they have filled their land with practices from the East
and with sorcerers, as the Philistines do.
They have made alliances with pagans.
NLT.7:
Israel is full of silver and gold;
there is no end to its treasures.
Their land is full of warhorses;
there is no end to its chariots.
NLT.8:
Their land is full of idols;
the people worship things they have made
with their own hands.
NLT.9:
So now they will be humbled,
and all will be brought low —
do not forgive them.
NLT.10:
Crawl into caves in the rocks.
Hide in the dust
from the terror of the LORD
and the glory of his majesty.
NLT.11:
Human pride will be brought down,
and human arrogance will be humbled.
Only the LORD will be exalted
on that day of judgment.
NLT.12:
For the LORD of Heaven’s Armies
has a day of reckoning.
He will punish the proud and mighty
and bring down everything that is exalted.
NLT.13:
He will cut down the tall cedars of Lebanon
and all the mighty oaks of Bashan.
NLT.14:
He will level all the high mountains
and all the lofty hills.
NLT.15:
He will break down every high tower
and every fortified wall.
NLT.16:
He will destroy all the great trading ships
and every magnificent vessel.
NLT.17:
Human pride will be humbled,
and human arrogance will be brought down.
Only the LORD will be exalted
on that day of judgment.
NLT.19:
When the LORD rises to shake the earth,
his enemies will crawl into holes in the ground.
They will hide in caves in the rocks
from the terror of the LORD
and the glory of his majesty.
NLT.20:
On that day of judgment they will abandon the gold and silver idols
they made for themselves to worship.
They will leave their gods to the rodents and bats,
NLT.21:
while they crawl away into caverns
and hide among the jagged rocks in the cliffs.
They will try to escape the terror of the LORD
and the glory of his majesty
as he rises to shake the earth.
NLT.22:
Don’t put your trust in mere humans.
They are as frail as breath.
What good are they?

WEB.1: This is what Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
WEB.2: It shall happen in the latter days, that the mountain of Yahweh’s house shall be established on the top of the mountains, and shall be raised above the hills; and all nations shall flow to it.
WEB.3: Many peoples shall go and say, “Come, let’s go up to the mountain of Yahweh, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” For out of Zion the law shall go out, and Yahweh’s word from Jerusalem.
WEB.4: He will judge between the nations, and will decide concerning many peoples; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.
WEB.5: House of Jacob, come, and let us walk in the light of Yahweh.
WEB.6: For you have forsaken your people, the house of Jacob, because they are filled from the east, with those who practice divination like the Philistines, and they clasp hands with the children of foreigners.
WEB.7: Their land is full of silver and gold, neither is there any end of their treasures. Their land also is full of horses, neither is there any end of their chariots.
WEB.8: Their land also is full of idols. They worship the work of their own hands, that which their own fingers have made.
WEB.9: Man is brought low, and mankind is humbled; therefore don’t forgive them.
WEB.10: Enter into the rock, and hide in the dust, from before the terror of Yahweh, and from the glory of his majesty.
WEB.11: The lofty looks of man will be brought low, the haughtiness of men will be bowed down, and Yahweh alone will be exalted in that day.
WEB.12: For there will be a day of Yahweh of Armies for all that is proud and haughty, and for all that is lifted up; and it shall be brought low:
WEB.13: For all the cedars of Lebanon, that are high and lifted up, for all the oaks of Bashan,
WEB.14: For all the high mountains, for all the hills that are lifted up,
WEB.15: For every lofty tower, for every fortified wall,
WEB.16: For all the ships of Tarshish, and for all pleasant imagery.
WEB.17: The loftiness of man shall be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men shall be brought low; and Yahweh alone shall be exalted in that day.
WEB.18: The idols shall utterly pass away.
WEB.19: Men shall go into the caves of the rocks, and into the holes of the earth, from before the terror of Yahweh, and from the glory of his majesty, when he arises to shake the earth mightily.
WEB.20: In that day, men shall cast away their idols of silver, and their idols of gold, which have been made for themselves to worship, to the moles and to the bats;
WEB.21: To go into the caverns of the rocks, and into the clefts of the ragged rocks, from before the terror of Yahweh, and from the glory of his majesty, when he arises to shake the earth mightily.
WEB.22: Stop trusting in man, whose breath is in his nostrils; for of what account is he?

AMP.1: The word [from God] which Isaiah son of Amoz saw [in a vision] concerning [the nation of] Judah and [its capital city] Jerusalem.
AMP.2:
Now it will come to pass that
In the last days
The mountain of the house of the LORD
Will be [firmly] established as the highest of the mountains,
And will be exalted above the hills;
And all the nations will stream to it.
AMP.3:
And many peoples shall come and say,
"Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD,
To the house (temple) of the God of Jacob;
That He may teach us His ways
And that we may walk in His paths."
For the law will go out from Zion
And the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
AMP.4:
And He will judge between the nations,
And will mediate [disputes] for many peoples;
And they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks.
Nation will not lift up the sword against nation,
And never again will they learn war.
AMP.5: O house of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the LORD.
AMP.6:
Most certainly [LORD] You have abandoned your people, the house of Jacob,
Because they are filled with influences from the east,
And they are soothsayers [who foretell] like the Philistines;
Also they strike bargains with the children of foreigners (pagans).
AMP.7:
Their land has also been filled with silver and gold
And there is no end to their treasures;
Their land has also been filled with horses
And there is no end to their chariots.
AMP.8:
Their land has also been filled with idols;
They worship the work of their hands,
That which their own fingers have made.
AMP.9:
So the common man has been humbled [before idols]
And the man of importance has been degraded,
Therefore do not forgive them [O LORD].
AMP.10:
Go among the rocks and hide in the dust
From the terror of the LORD and from the splendor of His majesty.
AMP.11:
The proud look of man will be degraded
And the arrogance of men will be humbled,
And the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.
AMP.12:
For the LORD of hosts will have a day of reckoning
Against all who are proud and arrogant
And against all who are lifted up,
That they may be degraded.
AMP.13:
And the wrath of God will be against all the cedars of Lebanon [west of the Jordan] that are high and lifted up,
Against all the oaks of Bashan [east of the Jordan],
AMP.14:
Against all the high mountains,
Against all the hills that are lifted up,
AMP.15:
Against every high tower,
Against every fortified wall,
AMP.16:
Against all the ships of Tarshish
And against all the beautiful craft.
AMP.17:
Then the pride of man will be humbled
And the arrogance of men will be degraded;
The LORD alone shall be exalted in that day,
AMP.18: And the idols will completely vanish (be abolished).
AMP.19:
They [the stricken, deprived of all in which they had trusted] will go into the caves of the rocks
And into the holes of the ground [fleeing]
From the terror and dread of the LORD
And from the splendor of His majesty,
When He arises to terrify the earth.
AMP.20:
In that day men will throw away to the moles and to the bats
Their idols of silver and their idols of gold,
Which they made for themselves [as objects] to worship,
AMP.21:
To go into the caverns of the rocks and into the clefts of the [ragged] cliffs [as they flee]
From the terror and dread of the LORD and the splendor of His majesty,
When He arises to terrify the earth.
AMP.22:
Stop regarding man, whose breath [of life] is in his nostrils [for so little time];
For why should he be esteemed?

MSG.1: The Message Isaiah got regarding Judah and Jerusalem:
MSG.2:
There's a day coming
when the mountain of God's House
Will be The Mountain—
solid, towering over all mountains.
All nations will river toward it,
people from all over set out for it.
MSG.3:
They'll say, "Come,
let's climb God's Mountain,
go to the House of the God of Jacob.
He'll show us the way he works
so we can live the way we're made."
Zion's the source of the revelation.
God's Message comes from Jerusalem.
MSG.4:
He'll settle things fairly between nations.
He'll make things right between many peoples.
They'll turn their swords into shovels,
their spears into hoes.
No more will nation fight nation;
they won't play war anymore.
MSG.5:
Come, family of Jacob,
let's live in the light of God.
MSG.6:
God, you've walked out on your family Jacob
because their world is full of hokey religion,
Philistine witchcraft, and pagan hocus-pocus,
MSG.7:
a world rolling in wealth,
Stuffed with things,
no end to its machines and gadgets,
MSG.8:
And gods—gods of all sorts and sizes.
These people make their own gods and worship what they make.
MSG.9:
A degenerate race, facedown in the gutter.
Don't bother with them! They're not worth forgiving!
MSG.10:
Head for the hills,
hide in the caves
From the terror of God,
from his dazzling presence.
MSG.11:
People with a big head are headed for a fall,
pretentious egos brought down a peg.
It's God alone at front-and-center
on the Day we're talking about,
MSG.12:
The Day that God-of-the-Angel-Armies
is matched against all big-talking rivals,
against all swaggering big names;
MSG.13:
Against all giant sequoias
hugely towering,
and against the expansive chestnut;
MSG.14:
Against Kilimanjaro and Annapurna,
against the ranges of Alps and Andes;
MSG.15:
Against every soaring skyscraper,
against all proud obelisks and statues;
MSG.16:
Against ocean-going luxury liners,
against elegant three-masted schooners.
MSG.17:
The swelled big heads will be punctured bladders,
the pretentious egos brought down to earth,
Leaving God alone at front-and-center
on the Day we're talking about.
MSG.18:
And all those sticks and stones
dressed up to look like gods
will be gone for good.
MSG.19:
Clamber into caves in the cliffs,
duck into any hole you can find.
Hide from the terror of God,
from his dazzling presence,
When he assumes his full stature on earth,
towering and terrifying.
MSG.20:
On that Day men and women will take
the sticks and stones
They've decked out in gold and silver
to look like gods and then worshiped,
And they will dump them
in any ditch or gully,
MSG.21:
Then run for rock caves
and cliff hideouts
To hide from the terror of God,
from his dazzling presence,
When he assumes his full stature on earth,
towering and terrifying.
MSG.22:
Quit scraping and fawning over mere humans,
so full of themselves, so full of hot air!
Can't you see there's nothing to them?

NIV.1:
The Mountain of the Lord
This is what Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem:
NIV.2:
In the last days
the mountain of the Lord’s temple will be established
as chief among the mountains;
it will be raised above the hills,
and all nations will stream to it.
NIV.3:
Many peoples will come and say,
“Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord,
to the house of the God of Jacob.
He will teach us his ways,
so that we may walk in his paths.”
The law will go out from Zion,
the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
NIV.4:
He will judge between the nations
and will settle disputes for many peoples.
They will beat their swords into plowshares
and their spears into pruning hooks.
Nation will not take up sword against nation,
nor will they train for war anymore.
NIV.5:
Come, O house of Jacob,
let us walk in the light of the Lord.
NIV.6:
The Day of the Lord
You have abandoned your people,
the house of Jacob.
They are full of superstitions from the East;
they practice divination like the Philistines
and clasp hands with pagans.
NIV.7:
Their land is full of silver and gold;
there is no end to their treasures.
Their land is full of horses;
there is no end to their chariots.
NIV.8:
Their land is full of idols;
they bow down to the work of their hands,
to what their fingers have made.
NIV.9:
So man will be brought low
and mankind humbled—
do not forgive them.
NIV.10:
Go into the rocks,
hide in the ground
from dread of the Lord
and the splendor of his majesty!
NIV.11:
The eyes of the arrogant man will be humbled
and the pride of men brought low;
the Lord alone will be exalted in that day.
NIV.12:
The Lord Almighty has a day in store
for all the proud and lofty,
for all that is exalted
(and they will be humbled),
NIV.13:
for all the cedars of Lebanon, tall and lofty,
and all the oaks of Bashan,
NIV.14:
for all the towering mountains
and all the high hills,
NIV.15:
for every lofty tower
and every fortified wall,
NIV.16:
for every trading ship
and every stately vessel.
NIV.17:
The arrogance of man will be brought low
and the pride of men humbled;
the Lord alone will be exalted in that day,
NIV.18: and the idols will totally disappear.
NIV.19:
Men will flee to caves in the rocks
and to holes in the ground
from dread of the Lord
and the splendor of his majesty,
when he rises to shake the earth.
NIV.20:
In that day men will throw away
to the rodents and bats
their idols of silver and idols of gold,
which they made to worship.
NIV.21:
They will flee to caverns in the rocks
and to the overhanging crags
from dread of the Lord
and the splendor of his majesty,
when he rises to shake the earth.
NIV.22:
Stop trusting in man,
who has but a breath in his nostrils.
Of what account is he?

NET.1: Here is the message about Judah and Jerusalem that was revealed to Isaiah son of Amoz.
NET.2: In the future the mountain of the LORD’s temple will endure as the most important of mountains, and will be the most prominent of hills. All the nations will stream to it,
NET.3: many peoples will come and say, “Come, let us go up to the LORD’s mountain, to the temple of the God of Jacob, so he can teach us his requirements, and we can follow his standards.” For Zion will be the center for moral instruction; the LORD will issue edicts from Jerusalem.
NET.4: He will judge disputes between nations; he will settle cases for many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks. Nations will not take up the sword against other nations, and they will no longer train for war.
NET.5: O descendants of Jacob, come, let us walk in the LORD’s guiding light.
NET.6: Indeed, O LORD, you have abandoned your people, the descendants of Jacob. For diviners from the east are everywhere; they consult omen readers like the Philistines do. Plenty of foreigners are around.
NET.7: Their land is full of gold and silver; there is no end to their wealth. Their land is full of horses; there is no end to their chariots.
NET.8: Their land is full of worthless idols; they worship the product of their own hands, what their own fingers have fashioned.
NET.9: Men bow down to them in homage, they lie flat on the ground in worship. Don’t spare them!
NET.10: Go up into the rocky cliffs, hide in the ground. Get away from the dreadful judgment of the LORD, from his royal splendor!
NET.11: Proud men will be brought low, arrogant men will be humiliated; the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.
NET.12: Indeed, the LORD who commands armies has planned a day of judgment, for all the high and mighty, for all who are proud — they will be humiliated;
NET.13: for all the cedars of Lebanon, that are so high and mighty, for all the oaks of Bashan;
NET.14: for all the tall mountains, for all the high hills,
NET.15: for every high tower, for every fortified wall,
NET.16: for all the large ships, for all the impressive ships.
NET.17: Proud men will be humiliated, arrogant men will be brought low; the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.
NET.18: The worthless idols will be completely eliminated.
NET.19: They will go into caves in the rocky cliffs and into holes in the ground, trying to escape the dreadful judgment of the LORD and his royal splendor, when he rises up to terrify the earth.
NET.20: At that time men will throw their silver and gold idols, which they made for themselves to worship, into the caves where rodents and bats live,
NET.21: so they themselves can go into the crevices of the rocky cliffs and the openings under the rocky overhangs, trying to escape the dreadful judgment of the LORD and his royal splendor, when he rises up to terrify the earth.
NET.22: Stop trusting in human beings, whose life’s breath is in their nostrils. For why should they be given special consideration?
